subject: 3-year split prepay & ramp exception request
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@summit.ai>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Intro: 3-yr prepay structure request & ramp smoothing

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for taking our call this morning. SummitAI is looking to lock in a multi-year prepay for inference capacity across our product lines. High level: 3-year term, $3.2M total committed spend, but we need a split-billing and gradual ramp in year 1 (we're forecasting 20% of committed usage in Q1, 40% in H2 Y1) — finance needs an invoice profile that doesn't accelerate too aggressively.

Two asks up front: can Redwood support (a) a 2/3/3 split by year with an annual escalator capped at 6% (they prefer fixed escalator), and (b) a 15% term discount for 3-year upfront relative to list? Procurement will also require a short mutual action plan and an audit clause.

I attached the requested schedule template for your convenience (see SummitAI_Requested_Schedule.xlsx). Please advise what approvals you need internally and any proposed contract language around ramp/downside protection.

- Sanjay
Head of Procurement
SummitAI, Inc.

Attachment: SummitAI_Requested_Schedule.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet, 18KB)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@summit.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro: 3-yr prepay structure request & ramp smoothing

Sanjay — appreciate the clear outline and the template.

Short answer: we can support a tiered prepay with a split-billing profile and a capped escalator, but the final term discount and invoicing cadence will need approvals from finance and a senior sales sign-off for the discount level.

Proposed next steps from our side:
- I am attaching a draft pricing summary for a 3-year, $3.2M commit with a 12% term discount (conservative starter) and two optional concession lanes (15% with a tight invoicing profile; 10% with a more flexible invoicing schedule). See Redwood_Pricing_3yr_Draft.pdf.
- Vivek and Marcus — can you review the escalator cap (6%) and the proposed invoicing splits (Year1: 25% upfront, remainder quarterly invoiced) and confirm whether we can approve a 15% exceptional discount if SummitAI agrees to annual net-30 invoicing instead of split billing?

Sanjay — if you can confirm the exact quarterly usage profile (the attached template helps), I’ll loop in legal to draft the mutual action plan and a DocuSign packet for signatures.

Thanks,
Rachel
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Pricing_3yr_Draft.pdf (PDF, 45KB)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@summit.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro: 3-yr prepay structure request & ramp smoothing

Thanks Rachel — quick thoughts from GTM:

1) Discount: I can approve up to 13% term discount w/o exec escalation if finance signs off on the invoicing cadence. 15% is above my standard delegated authority given the account size.
2) Escalator cap at 6% is acceptable, but we should add a minimum-usage floor for year 2 to protect unit economics (propose a 60% cumulative usage threshold by the start of Y2, otherwise we reserve the right to reprice).
3) The split billing (more gradual year1 recognition) is okay as a commercial concession, but we need a clean audit clause and an up-front statement of expected ramp.

Marcus — please confirm whether finance can accept annual net-30 invoices tied to committed drawdown vs. split quarterly invoices. If finance needs the split (as SummitAI requested), we will need to reduce the discount to 11% or require partial escrow.

Vivek
SVP, Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@summit.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro: 3-yr prepay structure request & ramp smoothing

Folks — finance review below. High-level: we can support the deal if three conditions are met:

1) Invoicing: prefer annual or semi-annual invoices tied to committed amounts. If SummitAI insists on split-billing in year 1, we need an addition to the contract that caps bad-debt exposure (escrow or joint custodial account) and a 2% uplift to the pricing (effectively lowering the discount).
2) Usage floor: agree to the 60% cumulative usage threshold by start of Y2; if not met, we will apply a one-time reconciliation to bring effective realized ARR to the agreed economics.
3) Accounting sign-off: legal & audit need a short paper trail showing SummitAI's forecast and a PO commitment.

Given that, finance can sign off on a max 12% term discount with split-billing and the escrow language; if SummitAI moves to annual prepay invoicing, we can stretch to 15% but require net-30 payment terms and 30-day payment SLAs in the contract.

Attachment: Finance_Risk_Summary.txt (text, 3KB)

Marcus Lin
Director, Finance Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@summit.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, procurement@summit.ai
Date: Mon, 6 Jul 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro: 3-yr prepay structure request & ramp smoothing

Sanjay / Nina — thanks for the patience while we reviewed internally. Summary / final ask from Redwood: 

- We can offer the 3-year commitment at a 15% term discount only if SummitAI agrees to annual prepay invoicing (single invoice per year, net-30) and the 60% cumulative usage floor by start of Y2.
- If SummitAI requires split-billing in year 1 as originally requested, the approved discount is 12% and we will add escrow language to the MSA. There will also be a 2% uplift to effective pricing to cover collection risk.
- Escalator: 6% cap agreed to either lane.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm which lane you prefer (Annual prepay + 15% OR Split billing + 12% + escrow).
2) If you confirm Annual prepay, I'll ask Legal to prepare a DocuSign packet and we can route through HubSpot (see link). If you prefer Split billing, Marcus will provide escrow language for the MSA and Legal will prepare amended invoicing terms.

Links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/record/67890 | DocuSign (placeholder): https://docusign.net/1234ABC

Attachments: Redwood_Pricing_3yr_FinalSummary.pdf (PDF, 58KB)

Appreciate it — happy to jump back on a call if you want to walk the two lanes.

Best,
Rachel Kim

Redwood Inference
